_label: ODYSSEY II: A5's state-vs-KV rule applied to the Resident shortlist. Advertised context is a MEMORY LIABILITY, not just a capability -- and for several candidates the KV cache at full context exceeds the model weights.
_evidence: MEASURED from config anatomy (layers, kv-heads, head_dim) with bf16 K+V, cross-referenced against measured stored weight sizes. No GPU.
rule_applied: R-ssm-state-vs-kv-crossover -- attention KV grows linearly with context while recurrent state is constant; the hybrid ratio, not model size, sets where the crossover falls.
formula: kv_bytes_per_token = 2 (K and V) * n_layer * n_kv_heads * head_dim * 2 (bf16)

FINDINGS.advertised_context_is_not_free: the working-LM-tier receipt observed that 6 of 8 candidates exceed the resident's 8192 context, two by 32x. That stands, but it is only half the picture: serving that context costs KV. Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B needs 24.0 GiB of KV at its advertised 262144 tokens on top of 56.9 GiB of weights; Qwen3-4B-Instruct needs 36.0 GiB at the same context against just 7.5 GiB of weights -- nearly 5x its own body. Context capability and context AFFORDABILITY are different claims and this session had only measured the first.
FINDINGS.the_GQA_outlier: Olmo-3-7B has NO grouped-query attention at all -- 32 KV heads against 32 attention heads -- giving 512 KiB/token, 8x the cheapest candidate. At its own 65536 context that is 32 GiB of KV against 13.6 GiB of weights. For a body its size it is the most expensive to serve here, and nothing about its parameter count reveals that: KV cost is set by kv_heads x head_dim x layers, not by params.
FINDINGS.cheapest_to_serve: LFM2.5-2.6B at 60.0 KiB/token -- and it is a conv/attention hybrid, so only 8 of its 30 layers carry attention at all. This is A5's rule paying off directly: the hybrid layer ratio sets the KV bill, which is why a 2.6B hybrid serves long context more cheaply than a 7B transformer.
FINDINGS.for_the_resident_decision: on the S003 metric (VERIFIED ACCEPTED WORK / WALL / MEMORY / RESOURCES) the MEMORY denominator must be weights + KV at the context actually used, not weights alone. At HCLI's real working context (~8k) every candidate is cheap (0.47-4.00 GiB); the differences only bite if long context is actually exercised. So the honest reading is that context reach is a real advantage over the incumbent's 8192 ceiling AND a cost that only materialises when used.
